about: COMPLY.0 legal register: every legal and platform obligation that applies to Cerid or to products built with it, one entry per instrument and article, with its jurisdiction, official primary source and the consolidated version read, the obligation in plain words, the products, data flows and channels it applies to, the check that proves it, its effective and sunset dates, a counsel-review flag, the owning rows and the next review. scripts/check-registers.py (the crd-check-registers CTest and repository step) fails a binding obligation without an active check, a lapsed review, an entry read from no primary source when its rows close and a topic without a Turkish entry. docs/design/registers.md is the contract; it shares the standards register's format, guard and review machinery.

snapshot.method: Refreshed on 2026-11-01 by scripts/register-review.py from the approved source plan (118 records; report docs/sessions/2026-11-01-legal-register-federal-register.md).

review.cadence: A light scan quarterly, after each yearly platform event (the April SDK rule, Google I/O, WWDC, the August target API rule) and after each dated effective day the register holds, and a full re-research every year or when a scan finds a pinned instrument amended; Official Gazette of Turkey, EUR-Lex and Steamworks announcements are recorded as runs with their triggering entries. Reviews propose ROADMAP amendments for the user and never edit rows.

entries.title: KVKK: processing conditions and special categories

instrument.name: Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)

entries.obligation: Process personal data only lawfully, for specified purposes, minimised and kept no longer than needed, on a condition of Article 5 (explicit consent or a listed ground) and the stricter Article 6 rules for special categories; delete, destroy or anonymise it when the purpose ends.

check.name: data inventory CTest: every flow declares its lawful basis per jurisdiction

entries.title: KVKK: the aydınlatma notice kept separate from explicit consent

instrument.name: Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)

entries.obligation: Inform the data subject (aydınlatma) when personal data is obtained, with the items Article 10 lists (the controller, the purposes, the recipients and why, the method and legal ground of collection and the Article 11 rights); explicit consent (Article 3) is specific, informed and freely given.

entries.title: KVKK: the Communiqué on the obligation to inform

instrument.name: Communiqué on the Procedures and Principles to be Followed in Fulfilling the Obligation to Inform

entries.obligation: Inform the data subject when the data is obtained, in every processing whatever its legal basis, without waiting for a request and again before a new purpose: the controller and its representative, a specific and explicit purpose, the recipient groups and the purpose of a transfer, the collection method (automated or not) and the legal basis among Articles 5-6 of Law No. 6698, and the rights of Article 11; in clear and plain language, without general, vague, incomplete or misleading statements, consistent with the Registry, and separately from any request for explicit consent; for data not obtained from the data subject, within a reasonable time, at the first contact or at the latest at the first transfer; and keep the proof that it was given.

entries.title: KVKK: data subject rights and the 30-day answer

instrument.name: Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)

entries.obligation: Answer access, correction, deletion and objection requests within 30 days at the latest, free of charge (a fee on the Board's tariff only where answering has its own cost), accepting or refusing each with reasons in writing or electronically; deletion reaches every store and backup window.

check.name: data subject request service tests (deletion reaches every store)

entries.title: KVKK: data security and breach notification to the Board

instrument.name: Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)

entries.obligation: Take the technical and administrative measures that keep personal data secure; notify the data subject and the Board of a breach as soon as possible (the Board set 72 hours).

check.name: breach-notification runbook rehearsal with per-regulator clocks

entries.title: KVKK: transfer abroad under Article 9 as amended by Law No. 7499

instrument.name: Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)

entries.obligation: Transfer personal data abroad only on a processing condition of Articles 5-6 and an adequacy decision (Article 9(1)); without one, on an appropriate safeguard while the data subject can exercise their rights and seek remedies in the destination (9(4): an agreement between public bodies or binding corporate rules approved by the Board, a standard contract the Board announced, or a written undertaking the Board permits), a standard contract being notified to the Authority within five business days of its signature (9(5)); else only incidentally in a case 9(6) lists; record each transfer and its mechanism.

check.name: transfer records CTest with standard-contract notification reminders

entries.title: KVKK: the By-Law on transfers of personal data abroad

instrument.name: By-Law on the Procedures and Principles for the Transfer of Personal Data Abroad

entries.obligation: Where personal data goes abroad on a standard contract, use the contract the Board announced unmodified (its Turkish text prevails), signed by the parties or their authorised signatories, and notify it to the Authority within five business days of the last signature, physically, by KEP or as the Board sets, with proof of the signatories' authority and notarised translations of documents in another language; the exporter notifies unless the contract names the party; a change of parties or contents, or the contract's end, is notified the same way.

check.name: transfer records CTest with standard-contract notification reminders

entries.title: KVKK: VERBIS registration of the data controller

instrument.name: Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (KVKK)

entries.obligation: Register the publisher in the Data Controllers Registry (VERBIS) when the Board's thresholds or the foreign controller rule require it, before processing starts.

entries.title: KVKK: the regulation on deletion, destruction and anonymisation

instrument.name: Regulation on the Deletion, Destruction or Anonymisation of Personal Data

entries.obligation: A controller that registers under Article 16 of Law No. 6698 keeps a retention and destruction policy with the contents Article 6 lists, in line with its processing inventory; once every processing condition of Articles 5-6 has ended, delete, destroy or anonymise the data at the first periodic destruction after that day (at most every six months; within three months for a controller without a policy) or, on the data subject's request, within thirty days, informing a third party it was transferred to; state the methods in the policy, record every destruction and keep the records for at least three years.

check.name: retention CTest: a flow outliving its retention fails

entries.title: Turkish Penal Code: personal data offences
entries.obligation: Never record personal data unlawfully (Article 135, half as much again for the special categories), give, disseminate or obtain it unlawfully (Article 136) or fail to destroy it when the legal periods end (Article 138); a company gets the security measures of Article 140, so the data inventory and deletion service make every processing step lawful and auditable.

entries.title: Cybersecurity Law No. 7545: incident and vulnerability reporting
entries.obligation: Report the vulnerabilities and cyber incidents found in the services a product offers to the Cybersecurity Presidency without delay, hand over the data and documents it requests in time, take the measures the legislation sets and keep systems, software and records open to its audits.

check.name: reporting workflow rehearsed against seeded incidents

entries.title: Cybersecurity Law No. 7545: permits for cybersecurity products
entries.obligation: Obtain the Cybersecurity Presidency's approval before operating as a cybersecurity company subject to certification or authorisation, and before exporting a cybersecurity product, system or service its procedures make subject to permit; notify it of a merger, division or share transfer of a company producing them, which needs its approval where control changes; classify every Cerid product against that definition first.

check.name: crd-check-registers: every export's cryptography inventory against its reviewed classification

entries.title: Turkish Penal Code: information-system offences
entries.obligation: The coordinated disclosure policy and its researcher safe harbour respect the offences of unauthorised access or remaining in a system and unlawful monitoring of its data transfers (Article 243), hindering or disrupting a system and altering, deleting or inserting its data (Article 244) and making, selling or holding a device, program or code made exclusively for these offences (Article 245/A); Cerid never asks a researcher to commit one, and its security tools are not made exclusively for them.

entries.title: Electronic Communications Law No. 5809: coded and encrypted communication
entries.obligation: Classify encryption in communication products against Article 39, under which the BTK sets the procedure for coded or encrypted communication within an electronic communication service, outside the radio systems reserved to the listed public bodies (breaching it is an offence, Article 63(6)), without key escrow or weakened end-to-end encryption.

check.name: crd-check-registers: every export's cryptography inventory against its reviewed classification

entries.title: BTK regulation on coded or encrypted communication

instrument.name: Regulation on the Procedures and Principles for Coded or Encrypted Communication within an Electronic Communication Service by Public Bodies and Natural and Legal Persons

entries.obligation: Before producing or importing a coded or encrypted communication device or system used within an electronic communication service, the producer applies to the BTK for a permit with the documents Article 5(2) lists (the crypto algorithm and keys, the key generation, distribution and loading modules and, where needed, the software or hardware that decrypts, and two samples), delivers the code or crypto to the BTK when the permit is granted (Article 7(1)), changes no hardware or software characteristic without approval (Article 7(3)), keeps the systems from unauthorised use (Article 8(1)) and reports the devices placed on the market by the last working day of the next month (Article 11); a system in a local area not using an operator's infrastructure needs no permit (Article 7(2)). Cerid's end-to-end encryption delivers no keys, so whether a product falls within the regulation is settled before a communication product operates in Turkey.

entries.title: Ministry of Trade dual-use export rules

instrument.name: Ministry of Trade communiqué on the export of dual-use and sensitive goods

entries.obligation: Identify the current communiqué and classify each export against its Category 5 Part 2 list.

check.name: classification record per product and release

entries.title: Turkey's asset freezes under Law No. 6415

instrument.name: Law No. 6415 on the Prevention of the Financing of Terrorism

entries.obligation: Screen distribution, accounts and payments against Turkey's asset-freeze decisions: the President's decisions implementing the UN Security Council lists (Article 5), foreign states' requests (Article 6) and domestic freezes (Article 7), each binding on its publication in the Official Gazette (Articles 11-12); make no transaction for a designated person and facilitate none (Article 13), report receivables and debts toward one to MASAK within 30 days (Article 12(3)), and never provide funds or financial services to one (Article 15).

entries.title: Turkey's proliferation-financing freezes under Law No. 7262

instrument.name: Law No. 7262 on the Prevention of the Financing of the Proliferation of Weapons of Mass Destruction

entries.obligation: Make no funds available to, and enter no business relationship in Turkey with, a person or entity the UN Security Council's proliferation-financing resolutions designate, or one it controls or that acts for it (Article 2(1)); apply each freeze, prohibition and lifting from the President's decision published in the Official Gazette, effective without delay (Article 3(1)-(2)), screening distribution, accounts and payments against the final lists the public bodies publish (Article 3(3)), the execution following Law No. 6415 (Article 3(4)).

entries.title: Law No. 5651: content, hosting and social network provider duties

instrument.name: Law No. 5651 on the Regulation of Publications on the Internet

entries.obligation: Act on removal and access-blocking orders within the legal deadlines, keep the provider records the law requires and meet the social network provider duties when a product reaches their thresholds.

entries.title: Law No. 5651: game-platform duties

instrument.name: Law No. 5651 on the Regulation of Publications on the Internet, as amended in 2026

entries.obligation: A game platform (infrastructure that exhibits, sells, distributes or runs digital games, manages licences or connects users) offers no game without its due age rating (an unrated game only at the highest age criterion) and removes unrated content, gives parents clear tools that control account settings and approve paid transactions, and gives the Authority the explanations it requests at once and within the period it sets of at most 15 days; a foreign-based platform above 100,000 daily accesses from Turkey also appoints and publishes a representative in Turkey.

check.name: 5651 game-platform kit CTests (parental payment approval, representative threshold monitoring)

entries.title: Law No. 5651: age ratings on game platforms

instrument.name: Law No. 5651 on the Regulation of Publications on the Internet, as amended in 2026

entries.obligation: Offer no game without its due age rating (an unrated game only at the highest age criterion) and produce the Turkish rating under the by-law the Authority issues on the rating criteria.

check.name: rating answers authored once generate every submission

entries.title: ICTA secondary rules for game platforms

instrument.name: ICTA (BTK) regulation under Law No. 5651 for game platforms

entries.obligation: Track the secondary rules ICTA issues for game platforms and pin them when published.

entries.title: Law No. 5651: the under-15 restriction on social networks

instrument.name: Law No. 5651 on the Regulation of Publications on the Internet, as amended in 2026

entries.obligation: Where a product meets the social network provider definition, serve no child under 15 (with age verification), serve children of 15 and over a separate service, publish the measures taken, give parents clear tools over account settings, paid transactions and usage time, and block deceptive advertising.

entries.title: Law No. 5809: authorisation for communication services
entries.obligation: Classify each communication product (voice, video, text) as an electronic communication service or not and, where it is one, notify the BTK before operating it in Turkey, with a usage right where it needs numbers, frequencies or satellite positions (Article 9(2)-(3); operating without notification is an offence, Article 63(1)).

check.name: classification record CTest per communication surface

entries.title: BTK authorisation regulation for the electronic communications sector

instrument.name: Authorisation Regulation for the Electronic Communications Sector

entries.obligation: Where a communication product is an electronic communication service in Turkey, offer it only through a company the BTK authorised: a joint-stock or limited company under Turkish law founded for that activity, its articles naming it, with the minimum paid-in capital and clean records of its shareholders and managers (Article 7); notify the BTK on its form before starting, in writing or with a secure electronic signature, and start once the BTK confirms the conditions are met (Article 8(1)-(2)), with a usage right as well where numbers, frequencies or satellite positions are needed (Article 5(3)); an unauthorised service is shut down (Article 22). A network for one's own premises and needs, offered to no third party and for no commercial purpose, needs no authorisation (Article 6).

check.name: classification record CTest per communication surface

entries.title: BTK rules on personal data in electronic communications

instrument.name: BTK regulation on processing and protecting personal data in the electronic communications sector

entries.obligation: Apply the sector rules on traffic and location data, retention and security to communication products operated in Turkey.

check.name: classification record CTest per communication surface

entries.title: Law No. 6112: internet broadcasting

instrument.name: Law No. 6112 on the Establishment of Radio and Television Enterprises and Their Media Services

entries.obligation: Classify live streaming against Article 29/A before offering it in Turkey: a media service provider offering radio, television or on-demand services only on the internet needs an RTÜK broadcast licence and a platform operator transmitting them a transmission authorisation, while individual communication, platforms not dedicated to transmitting such services and pure hosts are outside it (29/A(4)).

entries.title: RTÜK and BTK regulation on radio, television and on-demand services on the internet

instrument.name: Regulation on the Provision of Radio, Television and On-Demand Broadcasts on the Internet

entries.obligation: Where a feature offers radio, television or on-demand broadcasting online under editorial responsibility (individual communication, platforms not dedicated to transmitting broadcasts and hosting providers are outside the regulation, Article 2(2)), the media service provider holds an RTÜK internet broadcast licence (INTERNET-RD, INTERNET-TV or INTERNET-İBYH, a joint-stock company, ten years, Articles 5, 7 and 14) and a platform transmitting such services an internet transmission authorisation (a limited or joint-stock company, Articles 5(6) and 8), each meeting the duties of Articles 16-17 and the parental controls of Article 21.

entries.title: Law No. 6563: commercial electronic messages and IYS

instrument.name: Law No. 6563 on the Regulation of Electronic Commerce

entries.obligation: Send commercial electronic messages only with the recipient's prior consent, written or electronic (Article 6), recorded in the message management system (IYS), where a consent not transferred is invalid (Article 11(5)); each message matches its consent and identifies the sender with its contact details (Article 7), and carries an easy, free opt-out honoured within three business days (Article 8).

check.name: consent records CTest for commercial messages

entries.title: Law No. 6563: reporting to the e-commerce information system

instrument.name: Law No. 6563 on the Regulation of Electronic Commerce

entries.obligation: Report the information the Ministry of Trade requests for monitoring electronic commerce to the system it established (Article 11(4)).

entries.title: ETBIS registration under the e-commerce information system communiqué

instrument.name: Communiqué on the Electronic Commerce Information System and Notification Obligations

entries.obligation: Before trading, register the store in ETBIS through e-Devlet (its MERSİS and tax numbers, the domain and mobile application) as an intermediary service provider or a provider on its own platform (Article 5); within thirty days of registering, notify the Article 6 items (the KEP address, the kind of e-commerce, the goods and services, the payment methods and payment institutions, the infrastructure providers and the country and address of the databases holding personal and customer data); the annual cross-border volume by the end of each March, every change within thirty days and the end of the activity within thirty days (Article 7); as an intermediary, the Ministry's anonymised monthly statistics by the last day of the next month (Article 6(3)).

entries.title: Law No. 6502: distance contracts
entries.obligation: Before a distance contract, inform the consumer clearly of the items the regulation sets and that confirming the order creates a payment duty (Article 48(2), the burden of proof being the seller's); perform within the time promised, at most thirty days for goods (48(3)); honour the fourteen-day withdrawal right without reasons or penalty, extended up to a year when its information was missing (48(4)); a marketplace intermediary keeps a system open for the consumer's requests (48(5)) and shares the seller's liability for the pre-contract information and its records (48(6)).

check.name: checkout flow tests over the pre-contract steps

entries.title: The Regulation on Distance Contracts
entries.obligation: Before the consumer is bound, give every item of Article 5(1) (the seller's and the platform's identity, MERSİS or tax number and contact details, the total price with taxes, the withdrawal conditions or, for digital content delivered at once, that Article 15(1)(ğ) excludes the withdrawal right, the technical protection measures and the hardware and software the content works with) in writing or on a durable medium, in at least 12-point clear and plain language (Article 6(1)); show items (a), (d), (g) and (h) together immediately before the payment commitment and the delivery restrictions and accepted payment means before the order (Article 6(2)); have the consumer confirm receiving that information, or no contract is formed (Article 7); and state immediately before the order that it is an obligation to pay, or the consumer is not bound (Article 8(1)). The platform is jointly liable with the seller (Articles 5(7) and 6(6)); the withdrawal right otherwise lasts fourteen days (Article 9).

check.name: checkout flow tests over the pre-contract steps

entries.title: Law No. 5070 on electronic signatures
entries.obligation: Where a contract, invoice or developer agreement needs a written form, use a secure electronic signature (made with a secure signature-creation device on a qualified electronic certificate, Article 4), which Article 5 gives the legal effect of a handwritten one; a transaction the law subjects to an official form or ceremony, and a guarantee contract other than a bank letter of guarantee or a surety bond of an insurer established in Turkey, cannot be made with it.

entries.title: Law No. 5846: software as a work and licence form

instrument.name: Law No. 5846 on Intellectual and Artistic Works

entries.obligation: Treat software (with its preparatory design) and assets as works, though the ideas and principles under a program and its interfaces are not (Article 2); an employee's work made on duty is exercised by the employer unless a contract says otherwise (Article 18); licences and transfers are written and name each right granted (Article 52), a licensee passes a right on only with the author's written consent (Article 49), and third-party works are used only within their licence.

check.name: licence-policy CTest over every pin and package

entries.title: Industrial Property Law No. 6769
entries.obligation: Clear product names against registered trademarks, whose holder can stop an identical or confusingly similar sign on the same or similar goods and services and the unfair use of a well-known mark (Articles 7 and 29), and respect patents before release, including codec patents: a computer program as such is no invention, but a patented product or process is used only with the holder's consent (Articles 82(2)(c) and 85).

entries.title: Trademark filings for product names (TURKPATENT)
entries.obligation: File trademarks for product names with TURKPATENT before launch (protection comes only by registration, Article 7(1); one mark per application with its goods and services list, Article 11; ten years from the application, renewed in the six months before the term ends, Article 23).

entries.title: EU trademark filings for product names (EUIPO)

instrument.name: Regulation (EU) 2017/1001 on the European Union trade mark

entries.obligation: An EU trade mark exists only by registration (Article 6): file each product name's application at the EUIPO with the request, the applicant, the list of goods and services and a representation of the mark, paying the application fee within one month, which fixes the filing date (Articles 30-32), after clearing it against earlier marks, whose owners may oppose within three months of the application's publication (Article 46); put the mark to genuine use in the Union for the registered goods and services within five years of registration and never suspend it for five years, or it may be revoked (Articles 18 and 58(1)(a)); renew every 10 years from the filing date within the six months before expiry, or the six months after it with the late fee (Articles 52-53).

entries.title: Law No. 5378 on Persons with Disabilities

instrument.name: Law No. 5378 on Persons with Disabilities

entries.obligation: Make information services and information and communication technology accessible to persons with disabilities (Article 7) against the TSE accessibility standards (Article 3(1)(g)), and make the reasonable accommodations that keep storefronts and purchase flows free of discrimination (Article 4/A).

entries.title: VAT Law No. 3065 for digital sales
entries.obligation: Charge and declare VAT on store sales of goods and services performed or used in Turkey (Articles 1 and 6), at the rate the President sets under Article 28; as a provider without a residence, office or seat in Turkey selling electronic services to natural persons not registered for VAT, declare and pay it itself (Article 9(1), from 1 January 2018) under the Ministry's scope and procedure (the VAT No. 3 return).

check.name: tax calculation tests per sale type

entries.title: Digital service tax (Law No. 7194)

instrument.name: Law No. 7194 on the Digital Service Tax

entries.obligation: Monitor the thresholds (exempt while the previous year's revenue from in-scope services was below TRY 20 million in Turkey or EUR 750 million worldwide, counted for the consolidated group, Article 4) and declare the tax monthly, by the end of the following month (Article 6), on revenue from digital content sales including games and in-game purchases, platforms where users interact and intermediation (Article 1), at 7.5 % (Article 5) unless a Presidential decision sets the rate in force.

entries.title: Digital service tax rate: Presidential Decision No. 10767

instrument.name: Presidential Decision No. 10767 on the digital service tax rate

entries.obligation: Apply the digital service tax of Article 5(3) of Law No. 7194 at 5 % from 1 January 2026 and 2.5 % from 1 January 2027, on the revenue earned from 1 January 2026, as Presidential Decision No. 10767 (Official Gazette of 25 December 2025, No. 33118) sets.

entries.title: Tax Procedure Law No. 213: invoices and records
entries.obligation: Document every record of a dealing with a third party, a document missing a compulsory particular counting as never issued (Article 227); give an invoice for every sale or service to a merchant, a professional, a book-keeping farmer or an exempt tradesman, and to anyone else when the price exceeds the amount of Article 232 (revalued each year under Repeated Article 414) or the buyer asks (Article 232); the invoice carries its date and serial number, the issuer's name, business address, tax office and number, the customer's name and address (its tax office and number where it has them) and the goods or service with quantity, price and amount (Article 230), numbered in sequence, signed and issued within seven days of the delivery or service or the shorter time the Ministry sets, or it counts as never issued (Article 231); the Law's rules on books and documents bind electronic books, records and documents (Repeated Article 242); keep the documents for five years from the calendar year after the one they concern (Article 253) and produce them during that time on request, with every piece of information and password needed to read electronic records (Article 256).

entries.title: Tax Procedure Law General Communiqué No. 509: e-invoice and e-archive

instrument.name: Tax Procedure Law General Communiqué No. 509
instrument.article: Sections IV.1.4, IV.2, V.5.2, V.6-V.8 and VI

entries.obligation: Issue every store invoice as an e-Invoice to a buyer registered for e-Invoice and as an e-Archive Invoice to everyone else (section IV.2.1): a seller over the internet whose gross sales reach 500 thousand TL in a period from 2022 joins e-Invoice and, by the start of the seventh month after that period, e-Archive (sections IV.1.4(a)(4) and IV.2.4.2), and since 1 January 2026 a taxpayer outside e-Archive issues every invoice, whatever its amount, as an e-Archive Invoice through the Administration's portal or a licensed special integrator (section IV.2.4.3; 1 January 2027 for simple-procedure and business-account taxpayers). An internet sale's e-Archive Invoice carries the particulars of section IV.2.3, the issue time in hours and minutes (section V.5.2), the web address, payment method and day, the day the goods were sent or the service performed, a carrier for goods and the statement "Bu satış internet üzerinden yapılmıştır.", and is delivered electronically (section IV.2.4.5); report the e-Archive Invoices to the Administration signed and time-stamped in its published format (section V.8); issue on paper only in the failures section V.7 lists, each paper or missing invoice drawing the special irregularity fine of Article 353 of Law No. 213 (section V.6); keep the e-documents with their financial seal or electronic signature for the statutory period in electronic form inside Turkey (a secondary archive abroad allowed, a third-party archive only one the Administration licenses), able to display and print them on request (section VI).

entries.title: Law No. 6493 on payment services

instrument.name: Law No. 6493 on Payment and Security Settlement Systems, Payment Services and Electronic Money Institutions

entries.obligation: Collect payments only through a bank or a payment or electronic money institution licensed by the Central Bank (Articles 13(2), 14 and 18; acting without a licence is an offence, Article 28) and decide the merchant-of-record role so the store never provides an unlicensed payment service; a store credit or wallet usable only in the store's own network stays outside the law until the Central Bank brings it in by volume (Articles 12(2)(h) and 18(5)).

check.name: payment adapter tests against a licensed institution's sandbox

entries.title: KVKK recommendations on personal data in artificial intelligence

instrument.name: KVKK recommendations on the protection of personal data in the field of artificial intelligence

entries.obligation: Apply privacy by design, minimisation and impact assessment to AI features that process personal data.

entries.title: Turkey's artificial intelligence bill
entries.obligation: Track the bill and pin its duties once enacted.

entries.title: GDPR: principles, lawful basis, privacy by design and records
entries.obligation: Process personal data lawfully on an Article 6 basis (Article 9 for special categories), minimised and purpose-bound, with data protection by design and by default and a record of processing activities.

check.name: data inventory CTest: every flow declares its lawful basis per jurisdiction

entries.title: GDPR: children's consent
entries.obligation: Where consent is the basis for an information society service offered to a child, obtain the holder of parental responsibility's consent below the member state's age (13 to 16) with reasonable verification.

entries.title: GDPR: transparency and data subject rights
entries.obligation: Give transparent notices and honour access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability and objection within one month.

check.name: data subject request service tests (deletion reaches every store)

entries.title: GDPR: security and 72-hour breach notification
entries.obligation: Secure processing appropriately and notify the supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of a breach, and the data subjects when the risk is high.

check.name: breach-notification runbook rehearsal with per-regulator clocks

entries.title: GDPR: data protection impact assessments
entries.obligation: Assess high-risk processing (crash pools with memory contents, anti-cheat signals, children's data) before it starts.

entries.title: GDPR: transfers to third countries
entries.obligation: Transfer personal data outside the EEA only on an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards, recorded per flow, and choose server regions accordingly.

entries.title: EDPB Guidelines 01/2025 on pseudonymisation
entries.obligation: Pseudonymise crash and telemetry identifiers with keyed one-way functions whose keys stay separate; pseudonymised data remains personal data.

entries.title: ePrivacy Directive: storing and reading on devices
entries.obligation: Store or read identifiers on a user's device only with consent unless strictly necessary for the service the user asked for.

entries.title: CRA: reporting actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents
entries.obligation: Through ENISA's single reporting platform, notify the coordinating CSIRT and ENISA at once of every actively exploited vulnerability and severe incident in a product with digital elements on the EU market: an early warning within 24 hours, a notification within 72 hours and a final report (14 days after a corrective measure for a vulnerability, one month after the notification for an incident).

check.name: reporting workflow rehearsed against seeded incidents

entries.title: CRA: essential requirements, support period and SBOM
entries.obligation: Meet the essential cybersecurity requirements, declare a support period, keep an SBOM, handle vulnerabilities with coordinated disclosure and ship security updates for every product with digital elements.

check.name: release CTests: SBOM, declared support period and reporting contact

entries.title: CRA: reporting contact and ENISA platform account
entries.obligation: Hold the account on ENISA's single reporting platform the Article 14 notifications go through before 11 September 2026, and designate the single point of contact users report vulnerabilities to, easily identifiable, named in the user information and not limited to automated tools (Article 13(17), applying from 11 December 2027).

entries.title: NIS2 for services Cerid operates

questions.question: For each data flow Cerid products run (crash reports, telemetry, network identity, anti-cheat signals, accounts, payments, user content and communications), which processing condition of Article 5 of Law No. 6698 may the publisher rely on, which flows need explicit consent, and does any of them process special categories of personal data under Article 6 (for example voice recordings, or anti-cheat signals that could reveal health or biometric data)?

Does a layered in-product notice shown before the first upload, with explicit consent asked in a separate step and a refusal leaving the product fully usable, meet Articles 3, 5 and 10 of Law No. 6698, and which items must the first layer of the notice carry?
Does the same layered notice, with consent asked in a separate step, meet the Communiqué on the obligation to inform, and may the notice be shown in the product rather than at each collection?

Which technical and administrative measures does the Board expect under Article 12 of Law No. 6698 for crash dumps that may hold memory contents, and from which moment does the 72-hour breach notification run when a processor (the cloud host) detects the breach?
Which mechanism of Article 9 of Law No. 6698, as amended by Law No. 7499, covers transfers to the cloud regions outside Turkey that the crash pool, accounts and store use?
